text:
Sam: Hey team — first day! Trying to get my dev env working on an M1 Pro. following the onboarding guide but `asdf install python 3.11.4` fails during build with OpenSSL/linker errors. Tried brew but still seeing `clang: error: cannot find -lssl`. Anyone seen this?

Priya: Welcome Sam! :wave: Ping @devex for onboarding stuff. Quick q — did you `brew install openssl` (or openssl@1.1)?

Sam: I did `brew install openssl` and `asdf reshim` but the build still dies. Full-ish error snippet:```
clang: error: cannot find -lssl
ld: library not found for -lssl
configure: error: OpenSSL not found
```

Noah: On Apple Silicon the default brew openssl sometimes ends up as `openssl@3` or different path. Try installing `openssl@1.1` and set the build flags:```
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
asdf install python 3.11.4
```
Also make sure `/opt/homebrew/bin` is before `/usr/bin` in your `PATH` so the brew-provided tools are found.

Sam: ok tried that — build progressed but ended up with `pip` missing from the final install. I think asdf python uses pyenv under the hood? Not sure why pip didn't come out.

Priya: pip should be bundled. One gotcha: if you have `PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS` set it can change the build outputs. Also check `openssl` and `readline` installs.

Devex Bot: If you're on a Redwood laptop image, try `redwood-setup bootstrap` or consult the devex docs at https://redwood.ai/devex/bootstrap — also make sure 1Password CLI is unlocked if you use it for SSH keys.

Noah: Another thing — run `env | grep PYTHON` to see any build env vars. I once had `PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS="--enable-shared"` set and it produced a python without pip. If that is present, unset and rebuild. After successful build, `asdf reshim` so shims pick up the binaries.

Sam: That was it — I had `PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS="--enable-shared"` leftover from trying a local build. Unset, reinstalled, pip is there. Two follow-ups: 1) my dotfiles symlink `~/.envrc` but direnv keeps asking to allow. 2) SSH agent forwarding / git pushes to our enterprise remote are failing — who should I ping?

Priya: For direnv run `direnv allow` in the repo root (first time). Also ensure you have `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` in your `.zshrc` or `.bashrc` so the hook is loaded. If your dotfiles symlink is stale, `ls -la ~/.envrc` to confirm.

Noah: For SSH, check `~/.ssh/config` has `AddKeysToAgent yes` and that the key is loaded: `ssh-add -l`. On mac, `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (or use 1Password SSH agent). If you're using 1Password, unlock the CLI and ensure the agent is configured. If it's an enterprise git error (permission denied), ping `@platform-setup` or me directly.

Sam: Thanks — fixed both. Direnv needed the eval line added; I had an old symlink to a dotfiles path that was removed. SSH was a 1Password key permission issue. Everything's green now. :tada:

Priya: Nice! Pro tip — add a short `SETUP.md` to your dotfiles repo describing the exact steps you took (brew packages, env vars you set). Helps future new hires.

Sam: Will do, just pushed a tiny `SETUP.md` to my dotfiles. Appreciate the quick help, folks!

Noah: welcome aboard — reach out if anything else pops up.

Devex Bot: If you want a checklist, here's our quick checklist: `brew`, `asdf`, `direnv`, `1password-cli`, `ssh keys`, `docker desktop` (if you need containers). See https://redwood.ai/devex/checklist for details.
